gp.heading: Gross Profit
gp.text:
Bitcoin gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $298,300, a decrease of $168,914 as compared to $467,214 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease is due to significant decline in Bitcoin activities as we shift our focus towards HPC activities.

HPC gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $10,295,669, an increase of $9,306,078 as compared to $989,591 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is primarily due to a shift from marketplace to direct sales.

cor.text: Cost of revenues, exclusive of depreciation and amortization, reflect direct costs associated with the delivery of the Company’s products and services to its customers. These costs include electricity and infrastructure expenses associated with operating the Company’s mining facilities. Cost of revenues, exclusive of depreciation and amortization, also includes colocation and hosting costs related to GPU-based high-performance computing data centers, as well as fees paid to certain consultants. These costs exclude depreciation and amortization, which is presented as a separate line item

oi.text: Other income (expense), net consists of non-operating income and expenses not directly related to our core operations. This includes income (expense) from non-consolidating joint ventures, warrant liabilities, loss on issuance of convertible note, gain on sale of equity method investments, and gain on disposal of property and equipment. It also includes amortization of certain non-revenue-generating assets.

opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Bitcoin operating expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $1,036,578, an increase of $301,364 as compared to $735,214 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is driven by an increase in compensation costs primarily due to merit increases and the issuance of restricted stock units in September 2026.

HPC operating expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $20,145,993, an increase of $17,898,947 as compared to $2,247,046 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is driven by the pivot to focus on the HPC business.

sm.heading: Sales and marketing expenses
sm.text: Sales and marketing expenses include social media, advertising and marketing costs, marketing consultant costs, website costs and costs related to conferences and seminars. It also includes all expenses related to employee salaries, commissions, benefits, and other costs related to the sales and marketing functions such as productivity tools, and customer relationship management tools.

ga.heading: General and administrative expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses include salaries, benefits, and stock-based compensation expense, and other costs of departments serving administrative functions, such as executives, finance and accounting, and human resources. In addition, general and administrative expense includes non-personnel costs, such as professional fees, legal fees, accounting and finance advisory fees and other supporting corporate expenses not allocated to cost of revenues or sales and marketing. General and administrative expenses also include acquisition-related costs when incurred and costs associated with preparing to become and operating as a public company, such as audit, legal, and consulting fees, listing and exchange fees, directors' and officers' insurance, and investor relations. Costs incurred in connection with the Company's direct listing were expensed as incurred and are included in general and administrative expenses.

da_op.heading: Depreciation and amortization expense
da_op.text: Depreciation and amortization relates to long-lived assets and intangible assets used in the Company’s business and is presented separately from cost of revenues. Depreciation expense relates primarily to buildings and improvements, server equipment, miners, and mining related equipment. Amortization expense relates primarily to finance lease right-of-use assets, vendor relationships and trade name. Operating lease cost is recognized on a straight-line basis and is not included in depreciation and amortization.

pretax.text: Bitcoin net income before income taxes for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $9,994,855, an increase of $10,044,504 as compared to a net loss of $49,649 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is primarily due to the gain on sale of T20 during January 2026.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: The Company utilizes judgment and estimates in assessing the need for the valuation allowance related to deferred tax assets, including net operating loss carry-forwards. In the event the Company were to determine that it would not be able to realize all or part of its net deferred tax assets, an adjustment to the deferred tax assets would be charged to income in the period such determination was made.

net.text: Bitcoin net income before income taxes for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $9,994,855, an increase of $10,044,504 as compared to a net loss of $49,649 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase is primarily due to the gain on sale of T20 during January 2026.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities of $54,276,127 increased by $56,802,941 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to net cash used in operating activities of $2,526,814 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the increase in deferred revenue of $78,997,422 from up-front deposits received upon execution of new HPC revenue contracts and increases in accounts payable and accrued expenses, partially offset by an increase in accounts receivable of $30,908,614. The net loss of $86,835,488 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included significant non-cash items, primarily the loss on issuance of convertible notes, issuance of common stock for services, and depreciation and amortization, partially offset by non-cash fair value gains on the convertible notes.

sbc.heading: Stock-Based Compensation
sbc.text:
The Company grants stock options and restricted stock units (“RSUs”). Compensation cost is measured at the grant date and recognized over the requisite service period, so the estimates that most affect expense are made when an award is granted and are not remeasured afterward unless the award is modified. The Company expects stock-based compensation to increase as it grants additional RSUs and options.

The Company values stock options using the Black-Scholes option pricing model, which requires estimates of the fair value of the underlying common stock, expected volatility, expected term, the risk-free interest rate, and expected dividends. For options granted before the Company’s common stock was publicly traded, significant judgment was involved in determining the fair value of the Company’s common stock and the expected stock price volatility. The Company considered numerous objective and subjective factors to determine the fair value of the Company’s common stock such as, but not limited to, (i) contemporaneous third-party valuations of common stock; (ii) the rights and preferences of the Company’s preferred stock relative to common stock; (iii) the lack of marketability of common stock; (iv) developments in the business; and (v) the likelihood of achieving a liquidity event, such as an IPO or sale of the Company, given prevailing market conditions.

wc.text: Net cash provided by operating activities of $54,276,127 increased by $56,802,941 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to net cash used in operating activities of $2,526,814 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the increase in deferred revenue of $78,997,422 from up-front deposits received upon execution of new HPC revenue contracts and increases in accounts payable and accrued expenses, partially offset by an increase in accounts receivable of $30,908,614. The net loss of $86,835,488 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included significant non-cash items, primarily the loss on issuance of convertible notes, issuance of common stock for services, and depreciation and amortization, partially offset by non-cash fair value gains on the convertible notes.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities of $121,693,350 increased by $124,501,787 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to net cash provided by investing activities of $2,808,437 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by purchases of property and equipment of $137,021,298, compared to $1,226,323 in the prior year, to support the Company's buildout of its HPC infrastructure, and data center set up costs of $5,999,851, partially offset by proceeds of $16,722,407 from the sale of equity method investments. The prior year also included cash acquired in a business acquisition and distributions from equity method investments that did not recur in the current period.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text: Revenues are derived primarily from the provision of compute power, together with mining hosting services and bitcoin self-mining. The Company's compute power revenue is reported in its HPC segment, and its mining hosting and bitcoin self-mining revenue is reported in its Bitcoin segment. The Company provides compute power directly to end users, including under multi-year direct contracts, as well as to a marketplace. Marketplace revenue reflects the Company's contractual share of the marketplace's net revenue from its customers, 80% under the Company's agreement with RunPod, and direct contracts are priced on a fixed per-hour basis for each unit of compute power. The Company deploys and maintains its compute infrastructure primarily in colocation data center facilities, which provide the megawatt capacity supporting its high-performance computing operations, and makes that infrastructure available to customers for large-scale cloud processing.

intro.text: QumulusAI is a distributed AI cloud platform that delivers accelerated access to high-performance GPU compute. Through an inference-first, demand-led deployment model across a network of data center sites, QumulusAI brings compute closer to customer demand, helping AI teams and enterprises scale production AI workloads with speed, flexibility and control. By combining rapid deployment with flexible private cloud infrastructure, QumulusAI gives customers a faster, more adaptable path beyond the capacity constraints of traditional centralized and hyperscale cloud models. Learn more at QumulusAI.com.

In March 2023, the Company entered into a Limited Liability Company Interest Purchase Agreement with Turn Key Mountain, LLC and 913 Hero, LLC ("T20 Purchase Agreement") to acquire a 50.01 % ownership interest in T20 Mining Group, LLC (“T20”).
